text: In model theory, what does a first-order structure (model) M for a language L consist of?
choices: A set of axioms together with all their logical consequences
A non-empty domain together with interpretations of every constant, function, and relation symbol of L
A deductive system of inference rules for deriving theorems
A countable collection of sentences closed under provability
explanation: A structure is a non-empty domain |M| plus an interpretation of each constant (an element), each n-ary function symbol (a function on the domain), and each n-ary relation symbol (a relation on the domain). Options A and D describe a theory (a set of sentences), not a structure; option C describes a proof system, which is syntactic rather than semantic.
